claims.statement: A cube is a set of literals with no variable twice; a split of a cube by k >= 1 distinct variables outside it has 2^k sign children.
claims.limits: The cubeproof package also fixes a canonical form (literals sorted by variable), identities of cubes and splits and the bytes of the CNF of a cube, and bounds k by 20; the shared contract vectors (`tests/contracts/test_contract_vectors.py`) and `packages/cubeproof/tests/cnf/test_cp_cnf_cubecnf.py` check them. The proofs use none of this.

claims.statement: Every assignment that satisfies a cube satisfies exactly one of its children under a split; if every child is refuted, so is the cube.
claims.limits: The children of a split in the cubeproof package (bit j of child t gives the sign of the j-th variable) are checked by `tests/contracts/test_contract_vectors.py` and by `test_child_nodes_follow_the_bit_numbering` in `packages/cubeproof/tests/cnf/test_cp_cnf_cubecnf.py`. These test the implementation, not the lemma.

claims.statement: A cube tree: a tree of cubes in which every node that is not a leaf carries a split and has exactly its sign children; refuted when every leaf is.
The leaves of a cube tree divide its root into disjoint regions; a refuted cube tree refutes its root, and with the empty root the formula.
claims.limits: Certification rests on this proof. Software counterpart, not a proof: on random tiny formulas (at most 4 variables) with random split graphs, alternatives and models, the cubeproof certifier is checked by brute force -- proved formulas, closed roots and used leaves are unsatisfiable, and the open lists cover every satisfying assignment exactly once (`test_truthful_random_evidence` in `packages/cubeproof/tests/certify/test_cp_certify_truthful.py`). Exhaustive only for those tiny formulas.

claims.statement: A cube closed by recorded refutations and splits is the root of a refuted cube tree built from them, whatever alternatives were recorded.
claims.limits: Software counterpart, not a proof: the cubeproof certifier's closure and selection (a split needs every child closed, alternative splits, the smallest refutation or closed split selected, requested roots closed only literally) in `packages/cubeproof/tests/certify/`, and the independently written `tools/certify_min.py`, which must produce the same certificates (`tests/independent/test_min_scenarios.py`, `tests/independent/test_min_corpus.py`). Agreement of the two certifiers checks the evaluation of closure, not the honesty of the journals (paper: rem:attestation).

claims.statement: If each of the 59 formulas has a refuted cube tree with the empty root, no neighbourly polyhedron with twelve faces exists.
claims.limits: The corollary is conditional. Its hypothesis is faces12:campaign, which is open. A closed nonempty pilot root does not contribute to it (paper: rem:pilotroot).

claims.statement: A refuted cube tree with a nonempty root settles only that region, never the formula.
claims.limits: Software counterpart: a closed nonempty requested root leaves its formula open, and a closed ancestor does not close a requested root (`test_a_nonempty_pilot_root_closes_alone_while_the_formula_stays_open` and `test_a_closed_ancestor_does_not_close_a_requested_root` in `packages/cubeproof/tests/certify/test_cp_certify_scenarios.py`).

claims.limits: Whether the leaves have been verified independently is faces12:leaf-verification, which is open.

claims.limits: `tests/reference/ref_paper.py` is a second implementation by the same project, not a formal proof: it shows that the encoder emits the formula the article defines, including the tuples each quantifier ranges over and the signs. It reads from the encoder the clauses, the names of the variables and three choices among sound alternatives (the cut point of layer A, the pinned corner, the gauge brackets) and checks each for admissibility; the tests require the cut point and the pin to be the article's, and the larger end `z1` and the choice of gauge brackets are fixed by the pinned hashes of the formula bytes. That the reference was written from the article before the encoder was read is a statement about its origin that no test can show. It does not show that the article's lemmas are true; for the boundary and corner layers with twelve faces that rests on the proofs (paper: lem:B, lem:I, lem:parity, lem:onereflex), since no realization with twelve faces is known. A clause that every known realization happens to satisfy is caught only by the comparison with the article, which is why that comparison is exact.

claims.statement: Journals are self-checksummed hash chains (each record carries the hash of the one before it and its own), so an edited, removed, inserted or reordered record is detected, and a torn last line is recognized as a torn tail; a record is validated before it is written, and every reader validates every record it reads.

claims.statement: `cubeproof certify` reports a formula PROVED only when its empty cube is closed by admitted verified attempts and splits whose children are all closed, recorded in journals of the campaign it certifies. claims.statement: `cubeproof audit` recomputes the used leaves of a certificate, all of them or a deterministic seeded sample, from the journals the certificate is recomputed from: it regenerates each leaf CNF and compares its hash, proves the leaf again and has cake_lpr check the new proof, and in strict mode compares the proof hash with the recorded one. A different valid proof is a mismatch, an unexpected model an inconsistency; a sample says it is a sample; a tampered certificate is refused before anything runs; the audit writes only its own journal and resumes only its own plan.

claims.statement: The scheduler admits a task only within the declared memory, CPU and disk budgets, reserving per stage (solve, sealed proof, check, stream); a task the idle machine cannot hold is refused or fails preflight instead of waiting forever; checker arena exhaustion retries only the check with a larger arena; no verdict stops a run: a model or an anomaly is recorded and the other work goes on. Only a check the checker accepts closes a leaf.

claims.limits: Budgets are reservations against measured or declared capacity, not a promise of physical memory; the operating system can still kill a process. Proof size estimates guide retries and do not guarantee success.

claims.statement: Solver and checker run in their own process groups under `prlimit` caps, started through `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL`; an oversized proof, a flood of diagnostics or an expired deadline ends the attempt with a recorded cause and never counts as success.

claims.limits: The caps are per process, not a cgroup. The parent-death signal needs util-linux 2.33 or later and covers the tool itself, not a process the tool started (CaDiCaL and cake_lpr start none).
